parts.prompt:
Which description fits an electrode in an electrolytic cell?
A. An ionic liquid carrying charge between electrodes
B. An ion moving through the conducting solution
C. A separator preventing products from mixing
D. A conductor contacting the electrolyte
parts.canonical_answer:
D. A conductor contacting the electrolyte. An electrode carries electrons to or from the reaction boundary.
Distractor explanations: A: This describes the electrolyte, not an electrode. B: An ion is a charge carrier, not the external conductor. C: A separator is not the conductor transferring electrons at the electrolyte boundary.
marking_guidance: Correct option D (1). D. A conductor contacting the electrolyte. An electrode carries electrons to or from the reaction boundary. Distractor explanations: A: This describes the electrolyte, not an electrode. B: An ion is a charge carrier, not the external conductor. C: A separator is not the conductor transferring electrons at the electrolyte boundary. No mark for more than one selected option.

Why does molten sodium chloride conduct electricity?

B. Electrons move freely through the liquid salt
C. Neutral sodium atoms carry the current

Distractor explanations: B: Charge passes through molten salt by ions, not free electrons. C: The mobile carriers are charged ions, not neutral atoms. parts.prompt:
Why does dilute sulfuric acid give twice as much hydrogen as oxygen by volume during electrolysis with inert electrodes, at equal gas conditions?
A. Hydrogen molecules have twice oxygen’s volume at equal moles
B. The overall change is 2H2O → 2H2 + O2
C. The hydrogen electrode receives twice the current
D. Oxygen atoms carry twice as many hydrogen atoms
parts.canonical_answer:
B. The overall change is 2H2O → 2H2 + O2. The balanced overall equation gives a 2:1 gas amount ratio.
Distractor explanations: A: Equal gas amounts occupy equal volumes at the same conditions. C: The same current passes through both electrodes in the circuit. D: The volume ratio follows the balanced reaction, not this atomic description.
marking_guidance: Correct option B (1). B. The overall change is 2H2O → 2H2 + O2. The balanced overall equation gives a 2:1 gas amount ratio. Distractor explanations: A: Equal gas amounts occupy equal volumes at the same conditions. C: The same current passes through both electrodes in the circuit. D: The volume ratio follows the balanced reaction, not this atomic description. No mark for more than one selected option.

parts.prompt: Draw a labelled arrangement for teacher-supervised electrolysis of aqueous CuSO4 using separated carbon electrodes and a low-voltage DC supply. Include an inverted, initially water-filled tube to collect a small gas sample above the positive electrode. Keep the cell open to the atmosphere.
parts.canonical_answer: The DC positive lead connects to a carbon anode and the negative lead to a separate carbon cathode. Both dip into aqueous CuSO4 without touching. An inverted water-filled tube has its submerged open mouth over the anode so bubbles displace water; the connecting lead enters through the open mouth, not through glass. The beaker remains open.

parts.prompt: Plan a teacher-supervised comparison of carbon and copper anodes in aqueous CuSO4. Include a fair comparison, electrode-mass measurements, a gas test and a conclusion method. Both trials have copper cathodes and a low-voltage current-controlled supply.
parts.canonical_answer: Compare a carbon anode with a copper anode, using a copper cathode in each fresh CuSO4 sample. Keep solution concentration and volume, immersed electrode area and temperature the same. Set equal measured current for equal time. Clean, rinse and dry electrodes consistently and weigh before and after each run. Collect any anode gas separately and test with a glowing splint after disconnecting. Compare anode mass change and gas observations: a copper anode should lose mass while a carbon anode produces oxygen; both cathodes gain copper. Repeat to check consistency.

Same CuSO4 concentration and volume (1).
Equal measured current and electrolysis time (1).
Clean dry electrode masses before and after (1).
Collect and test anode gas (1).
